text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Disy leader Yiannakis Matsis is rushed to intensive care after a heart attack.
- The government agrees on a Dayton-style procedure to solve the Cyprus problem provided common ground is found on basic issues first.
- Turkish special agents were burning Greek forests.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash calls for negotiations through correspondence.
- Partial government concessions were not enough to avert a nurses strike.
- The government and employee organisations are promoting an anti-labour package on payment of cost of living allowances and collective working agreements.
- Disputes deepen in Disy party over member's insistence to stand as independents in forthcoming parliamentary elections.
- The government is determined to prosecute anyone involved in squandering public funds.
- Missiles and tanks will be purchased by the National Guard in a new five year development programme.
- Chaos is expected at four hospitals today from a nurses strike.
- The National Guard will purchase Mirage jets as part of its new five year development programme.
